text: Municipal Code Chapter 237 “Nathan Phillips Square” prohibits any person from lighting a fire on the Square. The Sunrise Ceremony on National Aboriginal/National Indigenous Persons Day (June 21 st each year) requires the use of an open flame to honour the tradition of this ceremony. As part of the ceremonial practice, there will be a lighting of the sacred fire by the Ceremony Conductor and Helpers, who will also be responsible for letting it burn out. A contained fire bowl will be provided. The Sacred Fire is a key part of traditional Aboriginal practice and protocol. The Sacred Fire is also the place where medicines are placed before, during or after the Ceremony. This component is part of the spiritual connection and practice and is an important part of the Sunrise Ceremony. Its incorporation in this event shows respect for Indigenous tradition. The City of Toronto wishes to honour…

City Council on May 22, 23 and 24, 2018, adopted the following: 1. City Council grant permission to the Director, Equality, Diversity and Human Rights to use open flame on Nathan Phillips Square as part of the Sunrise Ceremony each year on June 21st (National Aboriginal/Indigenous Persons Day), contingent upon satisfying any conditions placed by the Fire Marshal.
